Hi, everyone. My name is Carlos, and I am one of the volunteers who help the families in the housing pilot. I am retired, and I live in the building where the three apartments are. Every Monday, I meet the new families at the hospital and walk with them to the apartment. I show them the supermarket which sends the food, the pharmacy that is open all night, and the small park where the children play. Many families are very tired when they arrive. Some of them traveled for two days by bus. For me, the most important thing is simple: on the first night, nobody in our building eats dinner alone.

Hi Fernando, it's Sarah. I read the newsletter article that you sent me, and I loved it. The story about Lucia and Pedro is exactly the kind of story which the board in Texas wants to hear. I have two questions for our next call. First, how many families were able to use the apartments in the first two months? And second, who is the person that organizes the volunteers? In Texas, we have a social worker who does that, and it makes a big difference. Oh, and one more thing: can you send me a photo of the living room where the families eat together? Talk soon!
